title: Vinyl versus streaming: why physical records arrive incomplete
seoTitle: Vinyl vs streaming: why physical records arrive incomplete
subtitle: On August 4, 2026, fans report vinyl versions with missing tracks or mixes different from the digital ones.
excerpt: On August 4, 2026, fans of artists like Charli XCX, Olivia Rodrigo and Raye say vinyl records arrive missing parts of songs or with different versions.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
On August 4, 2026, fans of pop artists discovered that vinyl versions of recent albums arrive incomplete or different from those available on streaming services. The issue has recurred in releases by names such as Charli XCX, Olivia Rodrigo, Raye and others, generating complaints about transparency and quality.

Charli XCX and the collaboration with David Cronenberg

The track "No One Lasts Forever", the closing of the album Music, Fashion, Film, was announced as a complete vinyl version, but it does not include Cronenberg’s spoken contribution, present on Spotify and Apple Music platforms. Charli explained to the Tape Notes podcast that the vinyl audio needed to be delivered earlier and that "we didn’t get David in time", adding that "There’s actually a different version of the song on the vinyl, which we haven’t really spoken about yet.".

Olivia Rodrigo and cuts in tracks from the album "You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love"

Fans who ordered the album on vinyl reported unexpected edits in half of its tracks, with bridges, endings and other musical passages missing. The same pattern of shortened versions appears in other releases, such as Raye’s, who admitted that "the digital versions of some of these songs, some are quite different" and asked the audience to "embrace that because I tried my best".

Other releases with shortened versions

The first pressing of the album Hurry Up Tomorrow by The Weeknd contained only 11 of the 22 digital tracks, in addition to shorter mixes and missing guest appearances. The initial edition of Cowboy Carter by Beyoncé omitted five songs present in the digital version. Albums by Nicki Minaj ("Pink Friday 2") and Lil Wayne ("Tha Carter VI") were also released on vinyl with fewer tracks, possibly to avoid the costs of double or triple releases.

Production limitations and tight deadlines

Vinyl plants need to receive masterings and artwork at least six weeks in advance; elaborate packaging requires even more time. Ben Savage, manager at Skeleton Records, notes that "The more complicated the package, the more time it’ll take to manufacture". In contrast, digital platforms process files in five business days.

Fan reaction and market outlook

Consumers have felt misled. Animesh Khare, from Paris, said: "Learning that the vinyl version isn’t the complete record definitely makes me hesitate to purchase it" and called for more transparency. A Reddit user wrote: "I ride for Charli, I love her as an artist, but a bait-and-switch isn’t cool." In cases like Olivia Rodrigo’s, the online store stated that the vinyl "was received as intended" and refused a refund. Despite the criticism, the saturation of variants boosted vinyl sales in the United Kingdom to 7.6 million units the previous year, a 13.3 % growth according to the BPI, but Savage warns that "It’s ripping off fans" and that excess could lead to buyer fatigue and the bubble’s collapse.

With information from The Guardian.
